title: VPC per tenant versus pooled VPC
hook: Network isolation for SaaS ranges from one shared Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) with security group rules to a dedicated VPC (or AWS account) per tenant. The choice drives cost, compliance, and operational complexity.

blocks.text: Pooled VPC: all tenants share VPC, subnets, and compute; isolation is application-layer (tenant_id) plus security groups. VPC-per-tenant: each enterprise customer gets dedicated VPC, often in their own account via account vending. Hybrid: pooled app tier, dedicated data VPC connected via PrivateLink. SaaS Lens recommends pool for most, silo VPC for regulated enterprise.

entries.plainDefinition: One VPC hosts all tenant workloads

blocks.text: Healthcare and finance tenants demand network isolation proofs. Interviewers ask when VPC-per-tenant is worth 10x operational cost. Answer: compliance requirement or contractual isolation — not default.

blocks.title: Interview framing
blocks.body: Say: pooled VPC default for scale; VPC-per-tenant or account-per-tenant for enterprise compliance.

sections.heading: How it works step by step

items.title: Assess compliance needs
items.body: SOC2 pooled OK; some contracts require network isolation.

items.title: Design pooled baseline
items.body: Shared VPC, namespace isolation, SG segmentation per service tier.

items.title: Provision silo VPC on demand
items.body: Step Functions + CloudFormation vend VPC/account for enterprise signup.

items.title: Connect via TGW or PrivateLink
items.body: Hub-spoke or PrivateLink endpoint for silo data access from pooled app.

snippet.label: Pooled VPC baseline
snippet.code:
SharedVpc:
  Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
  Properties:
    CidrBlock: 10.0.0.0/16
    Tags:
      - Key: saas-model
        Value: pooled
snippet.explanation: Single VPC for multi-tenant compute — default SaaS pattern.

snippet.label: Per-tenant VPC stack
snippet.code:
TenantVpc:
  Type: AWS::EC2::VPC
  Properties:
    CidrBlock: !Ref TenantCidr
    Tags:
      - Key: tenant-id
        Value: !Ref TenantId
snippet.explanation: Vended on enterprise contract — IPAM allocates CIDR.

snippet.label: PrivateLink endpoint connection
snippet.explanation: Pooled app reaches silo tenant DB without public internet.

snippet.label: Step Functions vend tenant account
snippet.code:
ProvisionTenant:
  Type: AWS::StepFunctions::StateMachine
  Properties:
    Definition:
      StartAt: CreateAccount
      States:
        CreateAccount:
          Type: Task
          Resource: arn:aws:states:::aws-sdk:organizations:createAccount
          Next: DeployBaseline
snippet.explanation: Automate silo account + VPC provisioning on enterprise signup.

blocks.title: Cloud vs app patterns
rows: VPC per customer like Heroku private spaces

blocks.title: Pitfalls to avoid
blocks.body: VPC-per-tenant for 10k small customers — ops nightmare. Pooled VPC with no SG segmentation between services. CIDR overlap when vending tenant VPCs without IPAM.

blocks.text: How to prove it in production: enterprise onboarding provisions silo VPC in < 4 hours automated; pooled tier has zero cross-tenant network paths in penetration test.

blocks.title: What gets you rejected in interviews
blocks.body: VPC per tenant for all customers by default — rejected as cost-prohibitive. Strong answer: pooled default, silo for enterprise/regulatory, automated vending.

interviewTakeaways: Pooled VPC = shared network, app-layer tenant isolation.
VPC/account per tenant for enterprise compliance — automate provisioning.
Hybrid: pooled app + PrivateLink to silo data VPC.
60s: Default pooled VPC for scale. Enterprise gets vended VPC or account. IPAM for CIDR. PrivateLink connects hybrid. SaaS Lens guidance.
commonPitfalls: VPC per tenant for everyone — unsustainable ops at scale.
Strong answer: tiered network isolation aligned to contract and compliance.
No automation for silo provisioning — manual 2-week onboarding.

jsTsCorrelations.note: Pooled VPC like shared Node process — isolation is logical unless separate instances.
Dedicated VPC like separate deployment env — stronger boundary than namespace alone.
